messages:
maria.k: Heads up — deploy entering grace window for the routing change. Planning to flip the ff:routing-v2 toggle from 0% -> 2% now, then to 10% after the 15m health check.

deploy-bot: deploy/5678 started by maria.k at 2026-03-20T14:33:19Z — image=service@v2.4.1. Canary group: us-east-1a.

owen.s: copying release notes here: 
- routing v2: prefix caching improvements
- safety: fallback to v1 on 504s

katie.h: quick question — are we pinning model-serving to v2.4.1-only or allowing autoswap?

maria.k: pin model-serving=2.4.1 for this rollout. we don't want any autoswap until after full ramp. added note in release notes.

jason.t: health checks look good so far. error rate stable at baseline. recommend hold for 15m then 10% if still green. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary metrics (5m): latency +2%, error rate +0.1%, qps stable. Auto-rollback: disabled (manual for this release).

infra-bot: reminding: change window until 15:30 UTC, please avoid parallel infra changes.

maria.k: executing toggle command now:
```
redwood ff set ff:routing-v2 --percent 2 --comment "grace window initial"
```

katie.h: ack. I'll watch traces and tracing-slo dashboard.

oj: (typo, meant owen) owen.s: noticed one 5xx on a single host, investigating.

jason.t: if this is isolated, continue. set next step to 10% at +15m, 50% at +60m if green. Otherwise rollback to 0% and pin traffic to v1.

maria.k: agreed. manual rollback recipe in runbook: `redwood ff set ff:routing-v2 --percent 0` then `deploy-bot rollback deploy/5678 --to image=service@v2.4.0`

deploy-bot: deploy/5678 canary completed. current ff percent=2. Next scheduled action at 1987660099 (15m).

owen.s: added short note to release notes: "Do not enable auto-rollback for routing-v2 during first-week ramp."

katie.h: seeing a small spike in tail latency on two hosts, but traces point to greedy batch sizes in the model runtime. flag at 2% is low risk; if it grows by 0.5% error or latency +10% we preemptively rollback.

maria.k: thanks team. will call rollback if we hit either threshold. continuing monitoring. :eyes:
